question: In the United States, for Q4 2019 and Q4 2020, first select only those cities where total sales (with no promotions) rose by at least 20% from Q4 2019 to Q4 2020. Among these cities, rank products by their overall sales (still excluding promotions) in those quarters and take the top 20%. Then compute each top product’s share of total sales in Q4 2019 and Q4 2020 and calculate the difference in share from Q4 2019 to Q4 2020, returning the results in descending order of that share change.
sql:
-- Verify total sales per quarter for qualifying cities
WITH qualifying_cities AS (
    SELECT c.cust_city
    FROM sales s
    JOIN customers c ON s.cust_id = c.cust_id
    JOIN times t ON s.time_id = t.time_id
    JOIN countries co ON c.country_id = co.country_id
    WHERE co.country_name = 'United States of America'
      AND s.promo_id = 999
      AND t.calendar_quarter_number = 4
      AND t.calendar_year IN (2019, 2020)
    GROUP BY c.cust_city
    HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN t.calendar_year = 2020 THEN s.amount_sold ELSE 0 END) >= 
           1.2 * SUM(CASE WHEN t.calendar_year = 2019 THEN s.amount_sold ELSE 0 END)
)
SELECT 
    t.calendar_year, 
    SUM(s.amount_sold) as total_quarter_sales
FROM sales s
JOIN customers c ON s.cust_id = c.cust_id
JOIN times t ON s.time_id = t.time_id
JOIN countries co ON c.country_id = co.country_id
WHERE co.country_name = 'United States of America'
  AND s.promo_id = 999
  AND t.calendar_quarter_number = 4
  AND t.calendar_year IN (2019, 2020)
  AND c.cust_city IN (SELECT cust_city FROM qualifying_cities)
GROUP BY t.calendar_year
